subject: Human Evolution
title: The First Encounters
description: A quick, practical guide to The First Encounters.

hook.text: Around 100,000 years ago, Homo sapiens first walked into Neanderthal territory in the Near East.

buildup.text: Both species used similar tools and occupied similar caves—sometimes the same caves, centuries apart.

discovery.text: At some point, they didn't just coexist. They met. And some of them had children together.

twist.text: DNA proves interbreeding happened multiple times across tens of thousands of years—not as a single event.

climax.text: These weren't species that couldn't stand each other. Contact was repeated, sustained, and productive.

punchline.text: Different species met and chose closeness.

quiz.question: When did Homo sapiens and Neanderthals first encounter each other?
options: Around 100,000 years ago in the Near East
